sentences.text: Yurgovuchia is a genus of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaurs whose name means "coyote".
It is a smaller, distinct dromaeosaurid species with an estimated size of 2.5 meters.
Researchers identified this animal by unique skeletal traits including single pneumatopores on vertebrae, flexed cervical prezygapophyses, and a pubis lacking a pubic tubercle.
Fused vertebrae indicate that the single known specimen was an adult, not a juvenile Utahraptor.
The holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — was collected by Donald D. DeBlieux in 2005 from the Doelling's Bowl bone bed in Grand County, Utah.
Yurgovuchia was first described and named by Phil Senter and colleagues in 2012.
The generic name Yurgovuchia comes from the Ute word for coyote, a modern predator of similar size living in the same region.
The species name doellingi honors geologist Helmut Doelling for his decades of research and mapping in Utah.
Phylogenetic analysis places Yurgovuchia as an advanced dromaeosaurine closely related to Achillobator, Dromaeosaurus, and Utahraptor.
Yurgovuchia lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 130 million years ago in the Barremian stage.
The time range for Yurgovuchia is estimated from the Berriasian to Valanginian stages, between 139.1 and 132.6 million years ago.
Yurgovuchia lived alongside dinosaurs such as the theropods Falcarius and Geminiraptor, the sauropod Mierasaurus, and the large iguanodontian Iguanacolossus.
